# Overview

Driftwood is a duel between two harbours. Each player launches boats, piles cargo aboard and sails out to collect points, while a shared tide and a handful of squalls complicate the plan.

# Cards

## Boats

A boat card shows how much weight it can carry. Boats stay in your harbour until they sail out or are wrecked.

## Cargo

A cargo card shows its weight. Cargo is loaded onto a boat and scores points when that boat sails out.

## Squalls

A squall card shows a storm and no numbers. It is played from the hand to beach an opposing boat.

# Places

## Stock

The stock is the shared face-down pile. Nobody looks at it.

## Hand

Your hand is private. Keep no more than seven cards in it at the end of your turn.

## Harbour

The harbour is the public area where your boats and their cargo lie.

## Wreck pile

Spent cards go to the shared wreck pile, face up.

# The turn

A turn is four phases long. The player taking the turn performs them all.

## Ebb

1. Draw from the stock until you hold five cards.
2. If the stock has run out, shuffle the wreck pile face down and use it as the new stock.

## Sail

You may launch one boat by discarding a card from your hand. You may load cargo onto your boats. You may sail a loaded boat out.

## Flood

1. Move the tide marker up one mark, wrapping from the top mark to the bottom mark.
2. Starting with the player who is not taking the turn, each player may play one squall or pass.
3. When both players pass in a row, the phase ends.

## Moor

1. Discard down to seven cards.
2. Hand the turn to the other player.

# Boats and weight

A boat whose cargo outweighs its capacity is wrecked at once, together with everything aboard. Sailing out scores one point per unit of weight carried.

# Winning

1. In the Short Tide, ten points win the game.
2. In the Full Tide, twenty points win the game.
3. The game ends the moment a player reaches the target.
